title: Prepaid Credits + Fractional GPU Allocation — Scenario Sheet
body:
Overview:
This working sheet explores a coupling between prepaid customer credit packages and a fractional-GPU allocation offering (sell smaller time-slices / vGPU-style slices to teams). Purpose: quantify near-term runway impact, per-token cost delta, and hiring triggers when fractional allocation adoption increases across SMB customers.

Status & context:
- Draft; pulled from Q4 pricing experiments. Focus is on short-cycle (6–12 week) effects for ops and finance.
- Aligns to product ask: can we offer prepaid credits that map to fractional-GPU bundles rather than slot-based slabs?
- Key decision in next pricing forum Nov 16: whether to pilot 3-month prepaid credits tied to fractional pools.

Assumptions (base):
- Baseline token cost to Redwood (avg across fleets): $0.000018 per token (mix of quantized MPT-like variants and Llama derivatives).
- Fractional-GPU overhead: extra orchestration/packing cost = $0.9 / GPU-hour (ops + amortized infra).
- Typical fractional bundle sold: 50 GPU-hours equivalent/month.
- Prepaid discount tiers: 0% (pay-as-you-go), 10% (3-month), 18% (6-month), 25% (annual).
- Elasticity: prepaid buyers increase sustained utilization by 20–40% over month-to-month customers.
- Hiring: each additional 1.0 FTE SRE/Infra supports ~120 additional dedicated GPU-hours/day across regional pools.

Sheets / tabs (described):
1) Scenario summaries (text): baseline vs prepaid-heavy vs fractional-first.
2) Unit-econ rows: gross margin per 1M tokens, incremental GPU-hour cost, amortized orchestration.
3) Headcount phasing table (6, 12, 24 week): when to hire SRE / infra / capacity planners depending on GPU-hour growth.
4) Sensitivity matrix: prepaid price tilt (-10% to +10%) vs fractional overhead (0.5–1.5 $/GPU-hr).
5) Runway impact chart inputs: cash flow from prepaid receipts, deferred revenue, burn offset.

Key scenario snapshots (quick numbers, round):
- Baseline (no fractional, current mix): incremental margin per 1M tokens = $1,220.
- Prepaid-heavy (30% revenue moved to 3-month prepaid, fractional adoption 10%): incremental margin = $1,410 (+16%), but short-term deferred revenue increases by 18% of quarter receipts.
- Fractional-first (50% of SMBs choose fractional bundles tied to 3-month prepaid): margin = $1,650 (+35%), utilization smoothing reduces spot GPU spend by estimated 12%.

Headcount phasing (draft table text):
- Trigger A: Sustained +200 GPU-hrs/day for 3 weeks -> hire 0.5 SRE (contractor) or shift oncall coverage.
- Trigger B: Sustained +600 GPU-hrs/day for 6 weeks -> hire 1.0 Infra Eng (full-time) + 0.5 Capacity Planner.
- Trigger C: Fractional pools expansion to 3 regions -> hire 1 Cloud Ops + 1 Billing/Revenue ops engineer.

Sensitivity analysis notes:
- If prepaid discount moves from 10% -> 18% (more aggressive), adoption jumps but ARPU falls; need to model churn at renewal (assume 70% renew at 3 months).
- Fractional orchestration overhead is the biggest lever; if we can reduce it from $0.9 -> $0.4 /GPU-hr via packing improvements, margins improve substantially.
- Stress-case: prepaid heavy + high orchestration overhead -> short-term cash inflow but negative margin per token until amortization period (3–6 months) completes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we account for multi-tenant performance isolation SLO/penalty costs in fractional pools? (JIRA: JIRA-FIN-913)
- Need model of renewal/upgrade behavior for prepaid customers (ask Growth for cohort lift estimates).
- Validate orchestration overhead with Serving team: run microbenchmarks for packing efficiency on A100 vs H100.
- Legal: review revenue recognition for prepaid tied to capacity (linked: CONFLUENCE-REQ-4821).

Action items before pilot:
- [ ] Product: finalize fractional bundle definitions (50/100/200 GPU-hr equivalents).
- [ ] Serving runtime: deliver orchestration cost breakdown by hardware class (estimate by 2026-11-12).
- [ ] Finance: build cashflow stub for 3-month pilot projecting deferred revenue schedule.
- [ ] Sales/Growth: draft pilot offer text and expected uptake (target: 30 small-mid customers).

Quick sensitivity table (textual):
- Columns: fractional overhead ($0.5, $0.9, $1.3)
- Rows: prepaid discount (0%, 10%, 18%, 25%)
- Cells: delta margin per 1M tokens vs baseline; qualitative: red/orange/green flags.

Narrative summary (for exec slide):
- Prepaid credits mapped to fractional GPU bundles can smooth utilization and increase upfront cash, but margins hinge on orchestration overhead and renewal behavior. If orchestration overhead falls below ~$0.6 /GPU-hr and renewal >=70%, pilot yields net margin uplift and reduces spot spend. Otherwise, benefits are more cash/timing than structural unit economics.

References and rough links:
- packing-efficiency-bench (internal notes)
- CONFLUENCE-REQ-4821 (legal revenue-rec guidance)
- JIRA-FIN-913 (sensitivity mapping ticket)
- github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models/pulls/67 (model code for fractional allocation)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep scenario sheet lean; we will hand over to FP&A modeling once assumptions locked.
- Expect debate on whether to pass orchestration savings to customers (lower MR, higher adoption) or keep as margin.

End of sheet — comments inline welcome.
